I reproduced three remaining original-review cases on the exact `e3169d7` source merged through this PR. The maintained bounded-listing and First Prompt control passes. These follow-ups belong to the same #50643 contribution. The maintained implementation should keep its message-filename part keys, shared tool-state normalization, bounded listing/first-prompt reads, inline-content precedence and legacy JSON First Prompt routing.

The remaining review changes on the original branch address three behaviors:

1. **Separate-part freshness** ([original review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717073216)): [2c86f32e](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/commit/2c86f32e2447a3cdcdb74917fcedbe30507bc0bc) and its [atomic migration follow-up](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/commit/e6fa4c61b8b59656d8f1e41b15192fa9b5f8f7c6) track dependent message/part revisions across History, Search, persistent cache restarts and failed-version retries without changing the parent file's real stat or byte offsets. Exact-successor scenario: rewrite an assistant part at the same length while the parent session file is unchanged. **Observed:** after both persistent stores reopen, History still returns `draftquery` instead of `finalquery`, and Search returns 0 matches for the updated text. A later dependent revision also retains failCount 4 instead of receiving a fresh budget.

2. **Retry after ordinary part I/O failures** ([original review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717575059)): [89f916f0](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/commit/89f916f0c71f7a3a2d447ea666161f3afb07629d) separates failed reads from malformed JSON, and [92ef85ee](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/commit/92ef85ee48deca222c15db71d6ace24c8848fab8) keeps dependency failures from committing a complete replacement or exhausting the unchanged-version Search retry budget. Successfully read malformed JSON remains skippable. Exact-successor scenario: three required-part read refusals, persistent-store restart, then recovery with unchanged part stats. **Observed:** after the injected filesystem read refusals are removed, History still returns no recovered prompt. After three further refusals and reopening both stores, Search still returns `[]` instead of `['ses_retry']`; the part size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. The malformed-JSON skip control remains part of this scenario.

3. **Producer-order transcript emission** ([original review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717979274)): [51431a17](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/commit/51431a17d47ed1e590cb04fdd6109a4f5d9f39cc) emits consecutive text/reasoning runs around tool blocks only for legacy fallback parts. Full first-user prompt/preview extraction and the default inline/other-agent mode remain unchanged. Exact-successor scenario: reasoning → tool call/result → final text. **Observed:** the maintained file-backed parser still combines the final answer with earlier reasoning before the tool call/result. The correction expected by the original review produces six ordered emitted records instead of the current five combined records.

The original-branch candidate `51431a17d47ed1e590cb04fdd6109a4f5d9f39cc` passed its [complete required gate](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45981427909/job/140446017344) against `9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817`. That result validates the original-branch source, not the maintained successor.

**Exact-source verification:** [regression reproduction job](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45983920462/job/140454544058) checks out `e3169d781e15bf9e41f03b3caf4fb113604e4279` and verifies that no production source is modified. It reproduces three assertion failures and passes the unchanged maintained control: 12 part-directory reads for the bounded listing and one for the legacy JSON First Prompt. The job succeeds because these expected outcomes were confirmed; the three production scenarios remain failures.

The order check uses this PR's own fixture with only its expected emission order corrected. The freshness and repeated-I/O checks reuse the original branch's real discovery, persistence and SQLite Search probes. The record-ID directory case is deliberately excluded because this implementation uses filename keys. Import, module and setup failures are rejected as invalid evidence.

I am adapting the remaining corrections to current main while preserving this PR's filename-based storage boundary, shared tool-state normalization, bounded parsing and First Prompt routing. I will add the tested incremental candidate to this same comment.
commentBody:
## Follow-up on the same OpenCode contribution

This updates the existing handoff for #50643 and its merged continuation, #50781. The candidate adapts the three original review corrections to the maintained implementation and addresses the later [preview acceptance review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50781#discussion_r4718252235). It remains follow-up work on this contribution.

**Candidate source:** `981975040d7d71e231eb3c31965f9f0d5d9eb18f`, based on `6a8e7f533cf9f6e40afbc090ac35f42efb2e9b79`. [Immutable candidate diff](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/compare/6a8e7f533cf9f6e40afbc090ac35f42efb2e9b79...981975040d7d71e231eb3c31965f9f0d5d9eb18f). The exact candidate passed all seven focused tests and all 28 checks selected by the repository's complete required gate.

### Preserved maintained behavior

The adaptation keeps message-filename keys for part directories, filename ordering, shared OpenCode tool-state normalization, inline-content precedence, and the existing 100-message preview scan window. It also preserves the maintained legacy JSON First Prompt routing and its separate first-prompt read. The original record-ID directory case is not treated as a regression against this implementation.

### Historical reproduction on the merged source

The [exact-source reproduction job](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45983920462/job/140454544058) checked out `e3169d781e15bf9e41f03b3caf4fb113604e4279` and verified that production files were unchanged. It confirmed **three failing behavior scenarios and one passing maintainer control**:

- After a same-length assistant-part edit and reopening both persistent stores, History retained `draftquery` instead of `finalquery`, and Search found no updated text. A changed dependency revision also retained the previous failed-revision count.
- After repeated ordinary part-read refusals, removing the refusal did not recover the expected prompt/search result across store restarts, despite unchanged part size, mtime and ctime.
- The parser combined final text with earlier reasoning before the tool call/result, emitting five records where the expected producer order required six.

The bounded listing/First Prompt control passed: 12 part-directory reads for that listing fixture and one for First Prompt. The reproduction job succeeded because it confirmed those expected outcomes; the three production scenarios failed. The earlier [51431 complete gate](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45981427909/job/140446017344) applies to the original branch, not this adapted candidate.

### Dependency freshness and read recovery

For the [freshness review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717073216), a separate dependency signature records message/part metadata without altering the session file's real mtime, size or byte offsets. It participates in History cache reuse, persisted rows, Search read decisions, worker snapshots and failed-revision accounting. Additive schema changes remain transactional and preserve existing cached data.

After SQLite duplicates are excluded, discovery observes at most four retained legacy sessions concurrently. It enumerates message files and filename-keyed part directories, then records their metadata. Normal observation reads no message or part bodies. Only a part metadata failure triggers a message-body read to determine whether that dependency is used: inline content, another role or malformed JSON can make the inaccessible subtree irrelevant. Each message's part hash is incorporated only after successful observation.

This is **O(M + P) metadata work** for the observed messages and parts. The 12/1 control describes the parser fixture's bounded content-read path, not the total I/O of discovery.

For the [ordinary I/O review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717575059), filesystem refusals remain distinct from readable malformed JSON. Required source failures discard the incomplete Search replacement without advancing a complete cursor or exhausting the unchanged-revision retry budget. Malformed JSON remains skippable. The recovery scenario retains repeated failures, persistent-store reopening and unchanged-stat assertions.

### Emission order and visible preview counting

For the [order review](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/50643#discussion_r4717979274), only legacy OpenCode messages using nullish-content fallback opt into text/reasoning runs flushed around tool blocks. Default callers and inline messages keep their existing behavior; first-user prompt and preview extraction still use the whole decoded message. Each emitted run retains its **262,144 UTF-16 code-unit limit**. This is a per-run cap, not an aggregate per-message cap, so preserving separated runs can increase total retained text.

The preview cutoff now follows the same two-stage acceptance as the final preview consumer: `extractPreviewContentText`, then `normalizePreviewText`. A text block can become empty only at the second stage—for example, removing a hidden-context prefix can expose a standalone visual directive. Such blocks must not count toward the six visible previews used to stop the reverse scan. The 100-message window remains unchanged.

### Exact-source verification

The unused-directory/filename scenario now calls ordinary History listing through `scanAiVaultSessions`, with First Prompt checked separately through `readAiVaultFirstUserPrompt`. Both initial/updated preview assertions and the inline prompt assertion remain. The invisible-preview fixture separately retains its full-reader control and listing assertion. A test-only overlay on exact parent `d9a05c3882c493d04fbc521c6f4031b85f2babcb` reproduced a genuine listing assertion failure while its production files remained unchanged: the listing returned `[]` instead of `['Earlier useful preview.']`. The job then restored the exact final candidate before its passing checks.

- Exact-parent red proof: **confirmed** in the [same verification job](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45987772336/job/140467658038); one expected behavior assertion failed on `d9a05c38`, with no production overlay or setup/import failure.
- Final four-file run: **7 tests passed**, including the original freshness/repeated-I/O/order cases, default emission compatibility, unused-directory and filename behavior, the maintained bounded/First Prompt control and the strengthened preview fixture.
- Complete required `pnpm check:changed --base=6a8e7f533cf9f6e40afbc090ac35f42efb2e9b79 --maxWorkers=2`: **28 checks passed** in the [exact-source job](https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/actions/runs/45987772336/job/140467658038), including unit tests, typechecking, changed-code quality, formatting, lint, import boundaries, localization and the selected ratchets.

The job verified the candidate/base commit IDs and finished with tracked sources unchanged. These follow-ups are ready for review on the existing contribution; they are not an additional improvement count.
